solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Decent sale is arranged in store

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of the three words before it are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a respectable sale has been laid on in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges DECENT SALE IS; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli is a kind of shop selling prepared and imported foods.

clue.text: Delightful former lover absolutely saves lives

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: saves here means keeps safe inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: quite can mean absolutely, as in 'quite right'
lives in the sense 'exists' gives is

explanation.surface: An ex who is utterly delightful also rescues people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saves' reads as rescuing but signals one piece going inside another; 'lives' as a verb gives the short word.
explanation.definitionFit: Exquisite means extremely beautiful or refined, so a strong synonym for delightful.

clue.text: Picture the setter in ecstasy after publication

indicators.note: after places the setter-in-ecstasy pieces around the publication word so that it comes before IN and E

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as I
a mag is a magazine, a publication
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A setter delighted to see their work in print invites us to picture it.
explanation.walkthrough: E for ecstasy is the drug's street name.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to form a mental image of it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Mysterious phenomena crackpot partially recalled

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Strange happenings that some eccentric half-remembers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially' picks ENACRA from phenomENA CRAckpot and 'recalled' (called back) turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arcane is known only to a few, secret and obscure.

clue.text: John almost upset poet

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the letters are turned upside down, read bottom to top
almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: john is slang for a lavatory

explanation.surface: A man called John is nearly upsetting a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts TOILET to TOILE and 'upset' reverses it. 'John' looks like a first name but is US slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot (or George Eliot) is a famous writer of verse or novels; T. S. Eliot was a poet.

clue.text: Perhaps envy small home

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
at home is being in

explanation.surface: Possibly coveting a modest house.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is one of the seven deadly sins, an example of wrongdoing; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Unexpectedly, Ian Hislop beginning to like cosmetic product

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters of the name and the added letter are jumbled out of order
beginning to like means just the first letter of like is taken

explanation.surface: Surprisingly the satirist Ian Hislop has started to fancy some make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Hislop is a British satirist and editor of Private Eye. 'Unexpectedly' rearranges IANHISLOP plus L, the first letter picked by 'beginning to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacquer painted on fingernails is a beauty product.

clue.text: Media qualification holds water

indicators.note: holds says the answer sits inside the words just before it, across the word gap

explanation.surface: A media degree includes something about water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' hides the run in mediA QUAlification.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqua is the Latin word for water, used in English compounds and names.

clue.text: Greek character not in favour of red wine

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
anti means against, not in favour of

explanation.surface: A Greek man refuses to support a red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' reads as a person but is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red from Tuscany in Italy, an example of the drink.

clue.text: They're left prompts about answer

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the prompt word goes round the letter for answer

parts.note: prompts as a noun are reminders

explanation.surface: Notes that nudge you about a reply are left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts REMINDERS round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Remainders are what is left over, especially unsold books, so 'they're left' describes them.

clue.text: Number one trend in review issue

indicators.note: in review suggests looking back, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a tide is a trend or current of opinion

explanation.surface: A top fashion trend gets reviewed in a magazine issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in review' turns NO + I + TIDE (NOITIDE) back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue of a newspaper or magazine is one printing or version of it.

clue.text: Piece of advice to protect extremely unusual flower

indicators.note: to protect means the hint word wraps round and shields the other letters

parts.note: a tip is a helpful hint

indicators.note: extremely means the outer letters, first and last, of unusual

explanation.surface: A gardener is advised to guard a rare bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of advice' is the outer piece, and 'to protect' makes it wrap round the ends of unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: The tulip is a spring bulb bloom, an example of the class.

clue.text: Obtains top English painting

parts.note: lands means gets, as in landing a job
a cap is a top or lid

explanation.surface: Someone acquires a first-rate English picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' reads as an adjective (best) but gives CAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a picture of countryside scenery.

clue.text: Fully naked fat Irish gent emerged

indicators.note: fully naked says every one of the following words is stripped of its outer letters

explanation.surface: A stout Irishman stepped out without a stitch on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fully naked' takes the first and last letters off each of fat, Irish and gent, leaving A, RIS and EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Arisen means come up or appeared, the same as emerged.

clue.text: Most important part from officer on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard over the air, so the word is what the officer word sounds like

parts.note: a colonel is an army officer

explanation.surface: The key message comes from an officer broadcasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A kernel is the core or essence of something.

clue.text: Endless Royal Navy cuts elate criminal

indicators.note: cuts means the navy letters slice into the middle of the other word
criminal suggests something bent or wrong, so the letters of elate are rearranged

explanation.surface: The navy endlessly curbs the high spirits of a lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges elate into ETEAL, and 'cuts' slices the navy letters into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means without end, lasting forever.

clue.text: Street opera by Verdi returned in arenas

indicators.note: returned in a down clue means the opera name is read back the other way

parts.note: Aida is an opera by Giuseppe Verdi

explanation.surface: A street opera by Verdi is staged again in big venues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns AIDA into ADIA; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stadia is a plural of stadium, large sports grounds or arenas.

clue.text: European visiting friendly relative

indicators.note: visiting means the letter for European is staying inside the other word

parts.note: nice means pleasant, friendly

explanation.surface: A family member from the continent comes to stay and is pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visiting' puts E inside NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Your niece is your sibling's daughter, a family member.

clue.text: Keen on game, losing millions on the counter

indicators.note: on the counter means running against the direction, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: re means on, concerning

indicators.note: losing means the letter for millions is dropped

parts.note: taken as the word game

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic gambler loses millions over the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces without millions spell REGAE, which 'on the counter' turns round. 'counter' suggests a shop or betting counter, not reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager means enthusiastic, the same as keen.

clue.text: People who believe article in Sunday Times stigmatises, primarily

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: primarily means just the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece in the Sunday Times criticises believers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes the initials of in Sunday Times stigmatises: ISTS. The Sunday Times is a British weekly newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Theists hold faith in a god, so they are believers.

clue.text: Busy earl nagged cooks

parts.note: E is an abbreviation for earl in peerage lists

indicators.note: cooks means messes around with, so the letters of nagged are rearranged

explanation.surface: An occupied aristocrat pesters the kitchen staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooks' rearranges NAGGED to NGAGED. 'cooks' looks like a noun but is a verb meaning fiddles.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone line or a person that is engaged is occupied, the same as busy.

clue.text: Precious stone periodically gleams

indicators.note: periodically means taking letters at regular intervals, here every other one

explanation.surface: A jewel catches the light now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'periodically' takes the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of gleams.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem is a jewel, a valuable cut stone.

clue.text: Ultimately even the flea market is orderly

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: In the end even a flea market can be tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' takes the final letters of even, the, flea, market.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat means tidy and well arranged.

clue.text: Performed acrobatic feat second, sure to medal for a change

indicators.note: for a change means the letters of the following words are altered in order

explanation.surface: A gymnast flipped quickly, certain of a medal this time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges SURETOMEDAL after S.
explanation.definitionFit: Somersaulted means flipped head over heels, a gymnastic move.
